files are read and their comments are stripped first (an unescaped

starts a comment),
so a commented-out
is treated as plain text and never followed. The publication root is the file that contains
) and is not included by another file.

are then expanded recursively, with a cycle and depth guard.
Every file that is not reachable from the root is a redundant auxiliary file and is ignored, so the parse follows the selected compilation tree. This heuristic does not guarantee equivalence to a compiled PDF: unresolved includes are omitted and author macros are not expanded.

a block scanner finds sectioning commands, environments and display math.
The sectioning commands that actually occur in a paper are ranked (
part < chapter < section < subsection < subsubsection < paragraph < subparagraph

)
and mapped to consecutive levels, so the level of every heading is detected automatically: a paper that only uses

gets two heading levels.
The abstract becomes an

heading; unnumbered sections such as Acknowledgements and the appendices are kept;
the References section and the
The leaves of the tree are:
environments (a table is a kind of figure here) and stand-alone

and similar floats.
The LaTeX commands that define a figure (
children contain their own sentences, formulas and figures; lists can be nested.
Text is split into paragraphs on blank lines and then into sentences at

followed by whitespace and a capital letter, a backslash, a dollar sign or a quote.
A dot never splits a sentence inside mathematics or inside command arguments (

),
after single-letter initials, or inside decimal numbers.
A version stored as an empty record by Milestone 1 (PDF only, other formats) is recorded with the status

and produces no elements,
so the coverage statistics and the tables reflect reality.
Formatting commands without semantic content are removed (

, font-size and font-style switches, …),
as is the float placement option such as

are unwrapped in prose, and whitespace is normalized, so that
formatting differences do not make identical texts look different.

are converted to BibTeX entries with regular expressions:

segments, a quoted title, or sentence splitting
give the authors, title and venue, while the DOI, URL and year are matched separately; the entry type is inferred from the venue. The
are read by a small brace-aware parser. Each entry has a citation key, entry type, title, authors, year, DOI, journal and URL.

The entries of all versions of a publication (and the entries inside one version) are grouped with a union-find structure:
two entries are the same reference when they share a DOI, a normalized title, or a citation key with a compatible title.
One citation key is chosen for each group (the most frequent one, the newest version on ties), the

commands that use the dropped keys are renamed, and the fields of
the duplicates are
: the newest non-empty value wins, and missing fields fall back to older entries. This does not concatenate conflicting author lists. A non-
, even from an older version. Long normalized titles match without a year constraint; short non-empty titles require a year. The historical extraction used
and could discard later fields under the same key. The corrected
combines non-empty fields before cross-version unionization and retains conflicting values in
. These code fixes have not been applied to the historical corpus exports.
renaming, the identity of an element is its kind together with its cleaned text. Elements that match exactly across versions share one

table holds one node-parent edge per version. Repeated identical text inside a single version gets distinct ids,
so every version stays a tree.

Publications are processed in parallel by a pool of worker processes, with a configurable per-publication alarm on platforms supporting

. This timeout is not enforced by that mechanism on Windows, where this benchmark was measured. The status of each publication is saved periodically, so an interrupted run
resumes where it stopped.
